generators.name: hatch
generators.about: Parallel lines; crossed into a grid or a triad, joined into serpentines, dashed, bent, unevenly spaced, or thinned by tone.

options.doc: Families of lines: 1 parallel lines, 2 a grid (crossing at right angles), 3 a triad (at 60°).
Join the lines end to end into serpentines, so the pen lifts as little as possible (one family, no dashes).
Break the lines into dashes: `[on, off]` in mm.
How much dash and gap lengths differ, and how far each row's dashes are offset, 0 to 1.
How far the lines bend away from straight, in mm. Neighbouring lines bend together, like bedding.
The length of one bend along the lines, in mm.
How uneven the gaps between lines are, 0 (even) to 1: layered soil, worn bedding.
The tone across the area: even, denser toward the edge, toward the centre, in noisy patches, or along a gradient toward `toward` degrees.
How far the tone swings, 0 (none) to 1 (from full to nothing).
The scale of the tone: the width of the edge band, the size of noise patches, in mm.
With `density: "gradient"`: the direction the tone gets denser, in page degrees (90: down the page).

generators.name: scatter
generators.about: One mark at each of many places: dots, strokes, stones, plants or a symbol of your own, evenly scattered, on a lattice, in rows or in clusters, thinned by tone.

options.doc: Where the marks go: blue (even but irregular, like a stipple by hand), hex or square (a lattice; add jitter to loosen it), rows (along the angle, wandering only along their row: an orchard, a vineyard), clusters (small groups).
The mark: a symbol by name, or your own polylines in mm around the origin (up is negative y), drawn at their own size.
The size of one element: a dot's length, a symbol's height, in mm.

How marks turn: random (every mark its own way), aligned (with the pattern's angle), upright (standing up on the page whatever the angle: trees, reeds, crosses), or a number of degrees added to the pattern's angle.
How much element sizes differ, 0 (all alike) to 1.
How far elements wander from their place, 0 to 1.
Let marks overlap their neighbours. Off, a mark that would touch a neighbour gives way to it, as an engraver leaves symbols apart.
The tone across the area: even, denser toward the edge, toward the centre, in noisy patches, or along a gradient toward `toward` degrees.
How far the tone swings, 0 (none) to 1 (from full to nothing).
The scale of the tone: the width of the edge band, the size of noise patches, in mm.
With `density: "gradient"`: the direction the tone gets denser, in page degrees (90: down the page).

generators.name: cells
generators.about: Irregular cells: rounded stones apart from each other, a net of shared walls, or plates with wide cracks; with marks inside, sizes from even to mixed, thinned by tone.

options.doc: `stones`: every cell its own rounded outline, apart from its neighbours (gravel, cobbles, pebble beds). `net`: the shared walls, drawn once (cell nets, mud cracks seen from above, crazing). `cracks`: angular plates with wide cracks between them (dry cracked earth).
The space between neighbouring cells, in mm. Unset: 0.14 × spacing for stones, 0.24 × spacing for cracks; for a net, the break left where walls meet (unset: none, the walls join).
How rounded the corners are, 0 (sharp) to 1 (as round as the cell allows). Unset: 0.7 for stones, 0.25 for cracks.
How much element sizes differ, 0 (all alike) to 1.
How far elements wander from their place, 0 to 1.

A mark inside each cell: `dots` (a few specks: chalky soil), `hatch` (lines at each stone's own angle), `ring` (an inner outline: a rimmed pebble), `mixed` (terrazzo: some chips hatched, a few dense, most left plain).
The tone across the area: even, denser toward the edge, toward the centre, in noisy patches, or along a gradient toward `toward` degrees.
How far the tone swings, 0 (none) to 1 (from full to nothing).
The scale of the tone: the width of the edge band, the size of noise patches, in mm.
With `density: "gradient"`: the direction the tone gets denser, in page degrees (90: down the page).

generators.name: tile
generators.about: A motif laid on a lattice: brick, herringbone, basket weave, parquet, setts, flagstones, tiles, hexagons, stairs, grating, chess; your own polylines; or a CAD .pat hatch.

options.doc: What is laid: `brick` (running bond), `herringbone` (pavers at right angles in a zigzag), `basket` (pairs of pavers, alternating direction), `parquet` (square blocks of boards, alternating), `setts` (small stones in staggered courses), `flagstones` (random rectangular paving: course heights and stone lengths vary, joints staggered), `tiles` (square tiles with a grout joint), `hexagons` (hexagonal pavers), `stairs` (stone steps seen from above), `grate` (bar grating), `chess` (squares, alternate ones hatched); or your own polylines in mm around the origin.

One piece, `[length, width]` in mm. Unset, at spacing s: brick [3s, s], herringbone and basket [2s, s], parquet [4s, 0.8s] (a block of five boards), setts [1.15s, s], flagstones [3s, 2s], tiles and chess [3s, 3s], hexagons 2.5s across, stairs [6s, 1.5s] (slab length, tread depth), grate [3s, 0.5s] (cross bar pitch, bar pitch). For your own polylines: the tile box, centred on the origin (unset: the lines' extent).
For your own motif: how far each row is shifted along, as a share of the tile width (0.5: brick bond).

The joint between pieces, in mm: 0 draws single joint lines, each once; more draws every piece as its own outline, this far from its neighbours. Unset: 0.18 × width for setts, 0.1 × width for tiles, 0 for the rest.
How far elements wander from their place, 0 to 1.

A CAD hatch instead of a motif: a built-in name (ANSI31, ANSI32, ANSI33, ANSI37, BRICK, HERRINGBONE, BASKET, PARQUET, EARTH, CROSS, DASH, STAIRS, GRATE, ANGLE) or the text of a `.pat` definition. One pattern unit is `spacing` mm.

generators.name: waves
generators.about: Wavy parallel lines: sine, scallops, zigzag teeth, curling crests or a flowing swell; doubled into a net with `cross: 2`.

options.doc: How the lines wave: `sine`, the smooth classic; `scallop`, shallow arcs dipping between sharp cusps; `zigzag`, sharp straight teeth (amphibolite, schist); `curl`, crests that roll over into a spiral hook; `flow`, long swells the lines bunch and spread over, broken into strokes like a printed textile.
The length of one wave along the line, in mm. Default by shape, × spacing: sine 4 (3.6 with `cross: 2`), scallop 1.35, zigzag 1, curl 1.35, flow 13.

How far a line swings away from its row, in mm: a sine's or zigzag's peak, a scallop's dip, a curl's crest, a swell's height. Default by shape, × spacing: sine 0.25 (0.5 with `cross: 2`, so the net closes), scallop 0.35, zigzag 0.3, curl 0.27, flow 2.6.

1 one family of lines; 2 a net. Sine, zigzag and scallop add every row's mirror image, so crest meets trough and the lines close into cells (the ogee net, diamonds, eyes); curl and flow add a second family at right angles.
Sine, scallop, zigzag and curl: shift every other row along by this share of a wavelength (0.5 sets the cusps of one row over the middles of the next).
Turn the waves over: curls break the other way, scallops bulge up between downward cusps.
Scallop: the arc's shape, below 1 fuller and rounder, above 1 drawn to a point.
Curl: the size of the hook as a share of the amplitude. 1 rolls down onto the next wave's trough; smaller hooks hang above it.
Curl: how far each hook winds in, in turns (1 is one full turn).
Flow: how fast the swell's height and phase change from line to line across the sea (0 keeps one swell everywhere).
Flow: how broken the lines are, 0 (unbroken) to 1 (short strokes).

generators.name: rings
generators.about: Rings from the boundary inward, a spacing apart: concentric with the outline, offset from every edge, or one continuous spiral.

options.doc: What the rings follow: `outline`, the outer edge inset again and again (holes stop the rings; thin parts get a centreline); `edges`, every edge, holes included, each pushing rings of its own (a network of streets round blocks fills evenly).
One continuous path winding inward a spacing per lap, instead of closed rings: the fewest pen lifts. Follows the outline; holes cut it.

generators.name: scribble
generators.about: Hand shading with a fine pen: loose zigzag strokes with rounded turns, in overlapping patches, layered at different angles.

options.doc: Layers of scribble, each turned about 50° from the first: 1 a light shade, 3 the darkest.
How messy, 0 (tidy, even zigzags) to 1 (wandering ends, uneven passes, tilted patches).
The length of one pass of the pen, end to end, in mm.
The tone across the area: even, denser toward the edge, toward the centre, in noisy patches, or along a gradient toward `toward` degrees.
How far the tone swings, 0 (none) to 1 (from full to nothing).
The scale of the tone: the width of the edge band, the size of noise patches, in mm.
With `density: "gradient"`: the direction the tone gets denser, in page degrees (90: down the page).

generators.name: hilbert
generators.about: One unbroken space-filling Hilbert curve visiting the whole area cell by cell; cells between half a spacing and a spacing.

generators.name: truchet
generators.about: Truchet tiles: square cells a spacing wide, each with two quarter arcs turned at random, chaining into long winding paths.

generators.name: honeycomb
generators.about: Hexagonal cells a spacing across (flat to flat), each wall drawn once, or doubled `walls` apart.

options.doc: Draw every wall twice, this far apart, in mm (0: single walls, the hexagons touching).

generators.name: scales
generators.about: Fish scales: rows of half circles a spacing apart, each row resting on the tips of the one below; roof tiles and drawn water.

generators.name: sunburst
generators.about: Rays from a centre, about a spacing apart at every radius: new rays join in rings where the gaps open, so the centre never crowds.

options.doc: Where the rays come from, `[x, y]` in page mm. Default: the middle of the shape. Give the same centre to neighbouring areas and they share one burst.

generators.name: wood
generators.about: Wood grain: long lines a spacing apart running along the angle, wandering slowly and flowing round knots.

options.doc: How many knots the grain flows round, on average per square of 30 spacings (0: straight grain).

generators.name: marble
generators.about: Marble: veins about a spacing apart drifting across the slab at the angle, warped by turbulence, each drawn as its two edges so it pinches and swells.

generators.name: swells
generators.about: Overlapping swells or dunes: crest lines layered back to front, each hiding the ones behind and filled with lines that follow its slope.

generators.name: eddies
generators.about: Currents: evenly spaced streamlines of a flow that undulates and winds into spiral eddies.

generators.name: ripples
generators.about: Ripples: rows of broken wavy strokes a spacing apart, their crests bending together over a slow swell.

generators.name: canopy
generators.about: Tree canopies from above: clusters of wobbly lobes, a dot at each lobe's heart, trees a spacing apart.

generators.name: twigs
generators.about: Scattered twigs a spacing apart: a kinked stick with short side shoots at acute angles; brushwood, scrub, forest litter.

generators.name: doodle-trees
generators.about: Trees as a hand doodles them on a sketch map: each crown (a spacing across) one curly stroke round a lumpy circle, with a crescent of shade; nearer crowns hide those behind.

options.doc: The share of places that get a tree, 0 to 1: lower leaves clearings.
How many curls run round each crown's rim, as a multiple of the usual count.
The share of crowns with a crescent of shade on the side away from the light.
Where the light comes from, in page degrees (0: from the right, 90: from below; 225, the map maker's top left).

generators.name: growth
generators.about: Branches grown toward the space they have to fill (space colonisation): river deltas, veins, roots, cracks, lichen; twigs a spacing apart.

options.doc: How many roots the branches grow from (0: one per `root_spacing`).
Roots about this far apart, each draining its own basin, in mm.
How far a branch advances per step, in mm.
A point farther than this from every branch tip pulls nothing, in mm.
A point this close to a tip is reached and stops pulling, in mm.
How much each step wobbles off its course, 0 (straight) up.
The pen's width in mm: a trunk's extra passes sit this far apart, side by side (0 draws every branch as one line).
Most extra passes either side of a trunk: thick near the roots, a hairline at the twigs.
How far each tree reaches toward its neighbours, 0 to 1: below 1 leaves gaps between them.
How much trees differ in size, 0 (alike) to 1 (saplings beside big crowns).
A cap on growth steps, so a pathological shape cannot hang.

generators.name: isoline-stack
generators.about: Tree crowns drawn as stacked contour tiers, lit from one side; `spacing` is a crown's diameter, and the crowns are the mask.

options.doc: Shade the crowns with hatching on the side away from the light, for an engraved look. Changes the defaults: `light` 0.85, `hatch` 0.45 mm, `ticks` 0.65.
How patchy the crowns are, 0 to 1: low leaves clearings, 1 fills everywhere the shape allows.
The size of a leaf cluster on a crown's rim, in mm: smaller is lumpier.
Contour tiers through a crown: more draws more rings.
How ragged the contours are: 0 smooth boughs, 1.1 crisp leaves, 1.5 and up deep serrations.
The length of the contours' serration: lower is finer teeth, higher broad reaches.
Short slope ticks across the contours at bough clefts and in shade, 0 (none) to 1.5. Default 0.42; 0.65 when `hatched` or with a `hatch`.
How drawn out the crowns are, as if wind-swept, 0 (round) to 1.
How deep the clefts between boughs are, and how much a crown splits into sub-crowns.
How strong the sunlight is, 0 (none: every side alike) to 1: lit sides open up, shaded sides close in. Default 0.82; 0.85 when `hatched`.
Where the light comes from, in page degrees (0: from the right, 90: from below; 225, the map maker's top left).
How high the sun stands, in degrees: lower casts longer shade.
The shading hatch's spacing in mm, 0 for none. Default 0; 0.45 when `hatched`.

generators.name: isoline-blobs
generators.about: Blobs a spacing apart, each filled with nested contour rings like a height map; the blobs are the mask.

options.doc: The distance between nested contour lines inside a blob, in mm.
How much the field curls and drifts, 0 (round blobs) up.
The size of the warp's waves: lower is finer, higher broader.
Where ink begins on the field: higher keeps only the tallest blobs, lower fuses them into larger masses.

generators.name: clouds
generators.about: Cumulus seen from above: puffs a spacing across heaped on bodies that rise and fall, shaded away from the sun; the clouds are the mask.

options.doc: The size of the cloud masses and the clear sky between them, in mm.
The share of the sky that is cloud.
How much the masses curl and drift, 0 (plain blobs) to 1.
How closely the puffs crowd: about 0.6 few and round, 2 many and lumpy.
How drawn out each puff is along the run of its cloud, 0 (round) to 1.
How far the masses are drawn out along the wind (toward cloud streets).
The wind's direction on the page, in degrees (0: left to right).
Where the sun is, in page degrees (0: from the right, 90: from below; 225, the top left).
How high the sun stands, in degrees: lower shades more of each heap.
How tall the clouds heap up against their width: 1 a cumulus, 0.3 a flat sheet.
How much of the cloud is shaded, 0 (none) to 1.
The shade's spacing at its deepest, between dots or lines, in mm.
Shade in stippled `dots` (denser where deeper) or hatched `lines`.
Each shading dot's length, in mm (a pen's dot is a short stroke).

generators.name: solid
generators.about: A flat fill with no pen strokes: the host paints the area (an SVG fill, a screen preview); plotters draw nothing. Its mask is the whole area.
